newsitem.title: USA: More bizarre details emerge on UFO suicide cult.
newsitem.headline: More bizarre details emerge on UFO suicide cult.

text.p: Officials piecing together the grim story of the Heaven's Gate cult suicides on Friday released more bizarre details of a tragedy that has shocked the nation.

Among the new details were the fact that some of the males among the 39 victims had been castrated, and that one was the brother of a star of the 1960's "Star Trek" television series -- itself the object of a cult following among fans of science fiction and fantasy.

In a videotaped suicide note aired on Friday, members of the group explained how their deaths were part of a greater plan to join with space aliens they believed were following the comet Hale Bopp to Earth.
"We have no hesitation to leave this place, to leave the bodies that we have," Marshall Applewhite, the charismatic leader of the group and one of those who died, said on the video.
Coroners had completed autopsies on 30 of the victims by Friday afternoon, and planned to finish the rest over the weekend.
At a news conference on Friday, San Diego County Medical Examiner Dr. Brian Blackbourne said the bodies of the some of the male victims, including Applewhite, had been castrated.
He said, however, that the procedure had taken place some time ago and was not part of the elaborate suicide ritual.
Blackbourne also said that some of the victims died from suffocation rather than the deadly mix of phenobarbital and alcohol all had ingested.

Under a meticulous plan which dispatched the cult members in three separate groups, the victims ate pudding or apple sauce with drugs, washed it down with vodka and then put a plastic bag with elastic bands over their heads.
Blackbourne said the cycle of death occurred over a period of days and the first suicides probably took place last Saturday -- four days before the bodies were found.

As more details of the deaths emerged San Diego County Sheriff's Department Lt. Jerry Lipscomb said one of the focal points of the investigation was how the group obtained such large amounts of phenobarbital -- up to 50 tablets per victim.

The tragedy at the million dollar mansion north of San Diego touched nearby Hollywood on Friday with the revelation that one of the victims was Thomas Nichols, the brother of actress Nichelle Nichols, who played Lt. Uhura in the original "Star Trek" television series.
Nichols, 59, was one of two black members of the group. Two others were identified as Hispanic, and the rest were white.
The Star Trek connection seemed eerily appropriate, as the Heaven's Gate group had been said by acquaintances to be fans of the series about interstellar exploration.
"My brother was a highly intelligent and beautiful man. He made his choices and we respect those choices," Nichelle Nichols said on CNN's Larry King Live programme.

The two San Diego County Sheriff's deputies who were the first to enter the mansion on Wednesday made their first public appearance at Friday's news conference, telling reporters of their horrifying experience.

Deputies Laura Gacek and Robert Brunk described the smell of death even before they entered the mansion. "We could tell from the smell outside that we knew what we were going to find, but we just didn't know the magnitude, how many bodies or what condition they were going to be in," said Gacek.
Brunk, a deputy with six years in the department, said he recognised the smell of decaying flesh from other murder and suicide investigations.
The group, which designed computer web pages, sent two tapes to a former cult member and left two at the mansion in which their bodies were found.
According to the list the cult members came from California, Texas, New Mexico, Florida, Colorado, Arizona, Washington, Minnesota, Utah and Canada.
In the videotaped suicide note, cult members voiced confidence and happiness with their planned suicides, smiling and even laughing as they spoke to the camera.

"I'm about to take an act that probably this world would consider the most awful thing that any person could do," one man said. "We're going to be moving along to the next evolutionary level above human -- taking on a brand new vehicle that we're going to be using in the next level," another man said.
